expected_behavior: The relaunch request is rebuilt from scratch: the current executable, the fixed "runas" verb, and at most --elevation-restore=<validated hyphenated UUID> plus --elevation-workspace=<allowlisted workspace id>, with the child's working directory pinned to the install directory. A workspace without a ticket, a non-UUID ticket id, a NUL or secret-shaped argument all fail as UnsafeArgument; the parameter line follows Win32 quoting; a UAC cancellation (ERROR_CANCELLED) is reported as Cancelled rather than a failure, and any other ShellExecute failure is trimmed to 256 characters with secret-shaped text redacted.

notes: Extends CHROME-006.

title: Restore ticket is bounded, single-use, and expiring
user_story: As a security reviewer I want a tampered, stale, or replayed ticket to restore nothing.
expected_behavior: A ticket is written as {uuid}.json under the app-local-data elevation-restore directory and is refused when the id is not a lowercase hyphenated UUID, the entry is not a regular file (including a symlinked ticket), it exceeds 8 KiB, its schema version differs, its embedded id differs, it is older than five minutes (or dated in the future), it carries unknown fields, or its target fails revalidation. Claiming renames the file before reading so a racing process sees NotFound, the claim is removed even when the contents are invalid, and every rejection is reported as a bounded summary rather than a path.
entry_points: IPC restart_as_administrator (mint) and get_initial_elevation_restore (consume)
notes: Extends CHROME-030/CHROME-006; ticket I/O is offloaded to the blocking pool and the claim runs before the directory prune.

title: Startup claims the restore ticket before pruning, and never fails the launch

A failed restore therefore starts the app normally at its default view.

notes: Extends CHROME-030/CHROME-006.

title: Second launch raises the running window and hands over its files
user_story: As a user I want a double-clicked log to appear in the window I already have open, not a second window.
expected_behavior: A second launch is detected while the app is still being built so the stub window is never shown; the running "main" window is unminimized, shown and focused even when the launch carried no paths; the launch's paths are queued and second-launch-open is emitted without a payload. The window claims the queued paths on mount and on each announcement, taking-and-clearing them so a launch detected before the window was listening is still opened and no path is opened twice; a claim failure is logged and the next launch still opens.

notes: Extends CHROME-030; an elevated relaunch is excluded from the plugin because it replaces the process.

title: Forwarded launch arguments are parsed and resolved safely
user_story: As a user I want a relative path I typed in another directory to open the file I actually named.

entry_points: Second launch forwarded argv handled by the single-instance plugin
notes: Extends CHROME-030.

title: Forwarded opens are serialized so none is superseded

title: Recent list dedupes, caps at ten, and prunes
user_story: As an analyst I want a short Recent list that never offers something that is gone.
expected_behavior: Pushing promotes an existing (normalized path, workspace) pair to the front instead of duplicating it, keeps the same path in different workspaces as separate entries, and caps the list at ten entries by dropping the oldest. title: Oversized text is bounded without splitting code points
user_story: As a maintainer I want oversized evidence fields truncated safely and traceably.
expected_behavior: boundUtf8WithDigest returns the value unchanged when it already fits the byte limit; otherwise it returns a prefix cut on a code-point boundary plus a "…[truncated:<digest>]" suffix whose digest covers the full original value, replacing any lone surrogate left at the cut. expected_behavior: A tail batch is reported when it carries a reset, amendments, entries, a positive parseErrors or an observedThroughLine; the watcher emits it and the frontend logs the coverage-gap warning, so a batch that only reports malformed input or a framing overflow still reaches the session.

notes: Extends LOG-011.

title: Rotation or truncation rewinds the tail reader
user_story: As an analyst I want a rotated log to restart cleanly instead of showing the old run plus the new one.
expected_behavior: When the file size is smaller than the tracked byte offset the reader treats it as rotation: it discards pending Company Portal continuation state and pending input, rewinds to byte 0, restarts line numbers at 1 while keeping entry ids monotonic, and marks the batch reset=true so the frontend replaces rather than appends the view.
entry_points: live tail after a log rotation or truncation
notes: Extends LOG-011/CHROME-011; single-file resets replace everything, aggregate resets replace only that file.

title: Unterminated logical records are bounded and reported
user_story: As an analyst I want one runaway log line not to grow memory without limit while I watch a live log.
expected_behavior: A logical record that never terminates is bounded at 1 MiB (MAX_PENDING_LOGICAL_RECORD_BYTES); overflow discards the excess and reports a parse error naming the cap, and when the initial record's continuation overflows the reader discards bytes until the next newline so one physical line cannot be counted as many bounded fragments.
entry_points: live tail of Company Portal / Device Inventory logical-record logs
notes: Extends LOG-011; feeds the parse-error coverage count shown by the sidebar and quick stats.

title: Info pane decodes AppWorkload Get policies payloads
user_story: As an Intune engineer I want the app-policy JSON in a log line rendered as readable policy cards so that I can read intent, detection and scripts without eyeballing escapes.
expected_behavior: For a message starting "Get policies = " the info pane parses the JSON array (retrying with backslashes doubled when Windows paths contain invalid JSON escapes) and renders "N App Policy/Policies" cards showing Name/ID, Intent (Available, Available (no enrollment), Required, Uninstall), Target (User/Device/Both), Install and Uninstall command lines, Detection (Registry, MSI Product Code, File/Folder, PowerShell Script), Return Codes rendered as "<code>=<Failed|Success|Soft Reboot|Hard Reboot|Retry>", and for a PowerShell detection rule the base64-decoded ScriptBody inside the script viewer. A message that is not a policies payload renders nothing.
entry_points: info pane for an entry whose message starts with "Get policies = "
notes: Extends LOG-019.
test_method: e2e_browser: stories/log-view.spec.ts :: [LOG-096] the info pane decodes AppWorkload Get policies payloads

title: Info pane shows script-detection sidecar banners
user_story: As an Intune engineer I want the Win32 app detection sidecar lines summarised so that I can see whether the app was detected without parsing the raw text.
expected_behavior: A message mentioning SidecarScriptDetectionManager renders a coloured banner: "Script Detection Started", "Script Detection Complete", "PowerShell Exit Code" (green for exit code 0, red otherwise, showing "Exit Code: <n>"), "Detection Result" (showing "App Detected" or "Not Detected" from applicationdetectedbycurrentrule) or "Script Process" (showing "PID: <n>"); any other message containing the manager name renders the neutral "Script Detection" banner.
entry_points: info pane for sidecar script-detection entries
notes: Extends LOG-019; the detection banner derives only from the message text.
test_method: e2e_browser: stories/log-view.spec.ts :: [LOG-097] the info pane shows script-detection sidecar banners

title: Auto-detect the log format and return the resolved parser selection
user_story: As an analyst I want the app to choose the right parser for a file so that I never have to pick a format by hand.
expected_behavior: parse_content reads up to the first 20 non-empty lines (50 when the path hints at a DNS log) and selects a parser; the returned ParseResult carries formatDetected, the full parserSelection (parser, implementation, provenance, parseQuality, recordFraming, dateOrder, specialization), totalLines, parseErrors, filePath, fileSize and byteOffset. A file that matches no rule is read by the Plain parser with provenance Fallback and parse quality TextFallback, and format_detected maps each implementation to its LogFormat for the UI format column. Every one of the 22 ParserKind values has a contract name in the supported-format inventory.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file / parse_files_batch; status bar "Parser <label>"
notes: Extends LOG-001, which covers the coarse detect-and-parse behaviour; this row is the selection-metadata contract. Per-format framing/provenance is asserted by the parser_supported_formats text_contract_* tests.

title: Show the parser provenance, quality and framing of the open file
user_story: As an analyst I want to see how confident the parse is so that I know whether a file was read by a dedicated parser or a heuristic guess.
expected_behavior: getParserSelectionDisplay turns the backend selection into labels (parser name, implementation, Dedicated/Heuristic/Fallback provenance, Structured/Semi-structured/Text fallback quality, Physical lines/Logical records framing, Month-first/Day-first dates when the generic timestamped parser is used) and the status bar and info pane render them next to the file; a null selection renders nothing. For a folder stream the aggregate display reports the composition of the parsers that read its files and says the stream is mixed rather than adopting one file's format, and reports no display for a stream with no files.
entry_points: Status bar parser/provenance/quality segment; info pane; aggregate (folder open) status
notes: Extends CHROME-032 (status bar summary) with the parser-selection metadata contract produced by the parser crate.
test_method: component_test: reports the dedicated provenance an aggregate of dedicated parsers shares

title: Frame CCM records as logical records spanning physical lines
user_story: As an analyst I want a multi-line CCM message to stay one row so that stack traces and script bodies read as a single record.
expected_behavior: Lines containing <![LOG[….]LOG]!> (or the binary's fallback ` type="` plus component="` pair) select the CCM parser with provenance Dedicated, quality Structured and framing LogicalRecord; a message whose payload spans several physical lines becomes one entry whose message keeps the embedded line breaks and whose lineNumber is the record's first physical line. Text between matched records is emitted as its own plain-text entry with its own line number, and a file with no matches at all is re-parsed line by line.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on a CCM/SCCM log
notes: Framing is LogicalRecord in ResolvedParser::ccm() and asserted by text_contract_ccm (RecordFraming::LogicalRecord).

title: Map the CCM type field to severity
user_story: As an analyst I want CCM severity to come from the record's own type attribute so that the error count is trustworthy.
expected_behavior: type="0" renders Success, type="2" Warning, type="3" Error and any other numeric type Info; an absent, empty or unparseable type is left as None so severity falls back to message text rather than being coerced to Success, and an empty thread attribute parses as thread 0.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on a CCM/SCCM log; severity column
notes: Extends LOG-001's severity colouring with the exact type-field mapping.

title: Parse CCM timestamps with their own timezone offset
user_story: As an analyst I want CCM timestamps ordered by the offset the record carried so that a machine in another zone sorts correctly.
expected_behavior: time="HH:mm:ss.fff±TZO" plus date="MM-dd-yyyy" yields both an epoch from the stated offset and a display string of the record's own wall clock; a signed tail is always taken as the offset at face value (an out-of-range offset is reported invalid rather than reinterpreted) while an unsigned tail is fractional-second text and is never split into a fabricated offset. When no offset was written the epoch falls back to reading the stamp as UTC so ordering still works, and a midnight-crossing offset still yields the correct epoch.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on a CCM log; sortable timestamp column
notes: Timestamp display format is MM-dd-yyyy HH:mm:ss.fff as CMTrace renders it.

title: Parse Simple format with $$< delimiter
user_story: As an analyst I want legacy message$$<Component><timestamp><thread> logs to open with their fields split out.
expected_behavior: A line containing $$< selects the Simple parser (Dedicated, Structured, PhysicalLine); text before the delimiter is the message, the first <…> block is the component, and <MM-dd-yyyy HH:mm:ss.fff±TZ> plus the optional <thread=N (0xNNNN)> supply timestamp, thread and threadDisplay. Severity comes from the message text because the format has no type field, and the timezone offset is recorded on the entry.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on a Simple-format log
notes: Extends LOG-001 with the Simple grammar; detect.rs test_detect_simple covers selection.

title: Detect severity from message keywords when a format has no level field
user_story: As an analyst I want untyped lines ranked by their wording so that failures still stand out.
expected_behavior: A message containing "error", "exception", "critical" or "fatal" is Error; "fail" is Error but "failover" is excluded; "warn" is Warning; otherwise the line is Info. The check is case-insensitive and byte-level so it allocates nothing per line.
entry_points: Every parser without a level field (Simple, Plain, Timestamped, CmtLog fallback); severity column
notes: Shared fallback used by msg-based parsers; extends LOG-001's severity colouring.

title: Parse generic timestamped logs and keep unreadable lines visible
user_story: As an analyst I want ISO, slash-date, syslog and time-only lines recognised without losing the lines that are not.
expected_behavior: The generic timestamped parser tries ISO 8601 first, then slash-date, syslog and time-only, and caches the format of the previous matching line so later lines try that pattern first; a matching line yields a parsed message plus display timestamp, while a line matching nothing is still emitted as an entry (format Timestamped, no timestamp) and counted in parseErrors. A time-only stamp with an impossible clock is rejected rather than promoted.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on an unlabelled timestamped log; parse-errors count in the status/info surface
notes: Detection requires at least two timestamp matches in the sample (see the confidence row).

title: Resolve month-first versus day-first slash dates
user_story: As an analyst in a non-US locale I want 15/01/2024 read as day-first so that dates are not silently swapped.
expected_behavior: Slash dates default to MonthFirst, but when a sampled line's first field is greater than 12 the selection switches to DayFirst and dateOrder is reported as dayFirst in the selection metadata so the UI can label it. Explicit ISO and syslog dates are unambiguous and ignore the order setting.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file; status bar "Day-first dates" label
notes: dateOrder is serialized in ParserSelectionInfo and rendered by getDateOrderLabel.

title: Keep a zoneless wall clock and refuse an ambiguous one
user_story: As an analyst I want CBS/DISM timestamps to mean the clock the servicing host wrote so that the row order matches the text.
expected_behavior: CBS.log, dism.log and offset-less ReportingEvents rows are resolved through the machine's local zone instead of being promoted to UTC, so the epoch and the rendered timestamp agree. A wall clock that a DST gap or a fall-back repeat makes ambiguous resolves to no epoch at all — the record keeps its text and its display string but contributes no timestamp — because a guessed occurrence would reorder the surrounding records.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on CBS.log / dism.log / ReportingEvents.log
notes: Deliberate contract: a missing epoch is visible to every consumer, a wrong one is not.

title: Never fabricate a timestamp from malformed digits
user_story: As an analyst I want a log line with impossible digits kept as text instead of getting an invented timestamp.
expected_behavior: Timestamps are matched with ASCII-only digit classes, so a stamp containing Unicode digits (for example 14:30:00.١٢) or an out-of-range clock is not parsed; the line is preserved verbatim as a plain/timestamped entry with no timestamp, no display and no component, and it increments parseErrors. Valid non-ASCII text elsewhere in the same file (Café, Résumé, 日本語) is still parsed normally.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on a log with corrupt timestamps
notes: Regression suite for issue #413; covers timestamped, simple, ccm, cmtlog and reporting_events grammars.

title: Read plain text with no structured format
user_story: As an analyst I want any text file to open so that an unrecognised format is still searchable.
expected_behavior: When no rule matches, each non-blank line becomes a Plain-format entry with severity from its text, no component, no timestamp and no thread; blank lines are skipped without breaking entry ids, ids stay contiguous while lineNumber keeps pointing at the original physical line, and plain parsing never reports parse errors.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on any unrecognised text file
notes: Extends LOG-001's fallback path with the id/line-number contract.

title: Open empty, single-line and very large files without failing
user_story: As an analyst I want degenerate and oversized inputs to degrade to plain text rather than erroring.
expected_behavior: An empty file selects the Plain parser with zero entries and zero parse errors, a single unstructured line is parsed as Plain, a truncated CCM record is still recovered gracefully, a CCM record with a broken timestamp is kept as an entry, and a very large CCM log parses without panicking.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on an empty or truncated log
notes: Corpus fixtures live under src-tauri/tests/corpus/.

title: Parse CBS.log with continuation grouping and salvage
user_story: As an analyst I want CBS servicing records grouped and broken lines kept so that a partly damaged CBS.log is still readable.
expected_behavior: CBS is selected when a cbs.log path hint or \Logs\CBS\ hint is present and at least one record carries a CBS/CSI/TI/SR/SFC/RIBS/OC/POQ/SQM/DWLD component or an [SR] message; a well-formed header line starts a record, following non-header lines are appended to it as continuation text (with an embedded newline), and a line that has the date-time prefix shape but does not parse becomes its own fallback entry and increments parseErrors. The relaxed header accepts non-standard severity tokens and any component so DISM or other components interleaved in CBS.log still parse fully.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on CBS.log
notes: Framing is LogicalRecord (ResolvedParser::cbs()).

title: Parse dism.log as its own format
user_story: As an analyst I want DISM servicing output recognised on its own so that the parser column shows Dism rather than a guess.
expected_behavior: A dism.log path hint or \Logs\DISM\ hint plus at least one DISM-component record selects the Dism selection (dedicated, Semi-structured, LogicalRecord); without a path hint at least two DISM records are required. Records group continuations the same way CBS does, keep the DISM component, and a structurally-shaped but unparseable line is kept as a fallback entry counted in parseErrors.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on dism.log
notes: CBS and DISM share the log grammar; the selection distinguishes them.

title: Parse Panther setup logs with field enrichment
user_story: As an analyst I want Windows Setup records to expose their phase, operation and result code so that setup failures are triageable.
expected_behavior: A panther path hint (panther, setupact.log, setuperr.log) plus a PANTHER-format record selects the Panther selection (dedicated, Semi-structured, LogicalRecord); records with continuation lines are grouped, and the message is post-processed to lift a bracketed [Setup.exe] tag into sourceFile plus a component fallback, a C++ Class::method into sourceFile, PID/TID= into thread, Result=/Error:/Status: into resultCode, [gle=0x..] into gleCode, CurrentSetupPhase [..] into setupPhase and "Executing operation"/"Operation completed successfully" into operationName. Error and Fatal Error are Error, Warning is Warning, and Perf is Info.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on setupact.log / setuperr.log
notes: Extends LOG-001 with Panther; a missing component leaves component null rather than guessing.

title: Parse SoftwareDistribution ReportingEvents rows
user_story: As an analyst I want Windows Update history rows split into readable fields so that status and result code are explicit.
expected_behavior: A tab-delimited row with at least 11 fields, a GUID in field 1 and a parseable timestamp in field 2 selects the ReportingEvents parser (dedicated, Structured, PhysicalLine); the record GUID, event id, event name, update GUID, result code, provider and status become reader-facing fields, an opaque trailing agent token is dropped rather than shown as the message, and the message is composed as status | event name | operation | detail | HRESULT | EventId | Update. Severity follows the status field first (Success/Failure/Warning), then a set high bit in the result code, then a FAIL in the event name, then the message text; the timestamp uses the offset the record carried and is treated as a local wall clock when it carried none, and an unreadable result code is kept as written.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on ReportingEvents.log
notes: Placeholder GUIDs and the (null) provider token are normalised away; malformed rows fall back to a plain entry counted in parseErrors.

title: Parse MSI verbose logs with date carry-over and rollover
user_story: As an analyst I want msiexec /l*v logs to show engine context, action results and the final exit code.
expected_behavior: Weighted MSI signals (verbose-logging header, engine [PID:TID] lines, Action start/ended, Property dumps, MainEngineThread) select the Msi selection when at least two are seen; the context letter becomes MSI-client/server/action/nested, the header's M/D/YYYY date is applied to later time-only lines, and a time that jumps backwards by more than 23 hours advances the carried date for midnight rollover. Action-ended return values map 2/4 to Warning and 3 to Error, MainEngineThread exit codes map 0/1707/3010 to Info, 1602/1625/1638 to Warning and the 1600-range failures to Error (with 1600..1700 as Error by default), the footer is labelled MSI-header, and unrecognised lines are kept as plain text while still being counted as errors.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on an msiexec /l*v log
notes: Selection date order is MonthFirst because the header writes M/D/YYYY.

title: Parse WiX/Burn bootstrapper logs
user_story: As an analyst I want bundle logs to show their severity letter, message code and process/thread pair.
expected_behavior: Lines shaped [PID:TID][YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS]<i|w|e>NNN: message select the Burn selection once two are seen; the letter maps i→Info, w→Warning, e→Error, the component is the letter plus the three-digit code (for example i001), the thread is the PID with threadDisplay as "PID:TID" in hex, and the display timestamp is the ISO stamp with a .000 millisecond tail. Non-matching lines fall back to plain text with keyword severity.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on a Burn/bundle log
notes: Timestamps carry no offset in this grammar and are read as UTC.

title: Parse PatchMyPC detection script logs
user_story: As an analyst I want third-party patch detection output to show whether an app was found and in which context.
expected_behavior: A tilde-delimited row MM/DD/YYYY HH:MM:SS~[app]~[Found:True|False]~[Purpose:..]~[Context:..]~[Hive:..] selects the PatchMyPcDetection parser once two are seen (MonthFirst dates); Found:True is Info and Found:False is Warning, the message is composed as "[purpose] app — Found:x", the component is PatchMyPC, operationName carries the purpose and hostName carries the context with its trailing $) stripped.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on a detection script log
notes: These files are typically UTF-16LE; the encoding layer decodes them before this parser sees them.

title: Parse Secure Boot certificate update logs
user_story: As an analyst I want Secure Boot update script output to show its script tag and level.
expected_behavior: Lines shaped YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS [SCRIPT] [LEVEL] message select the SecureBootLog parser (dedicated, PhysicalLine); ERROR is Error, WARNING is Warning, SUCCESS is Success and INFO/SYSTEM are Info, and the component is the script tag (for example DETECT). A line whose date-time text does not form a real calendar value does not match, so it is kept as a Plain entry with no timestamp and counted as a parse error.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on SecureBootCertificateUpdate.log
notes: Selection needs the securebootcertificateupdate path hint plus one record, or two records without the hint.

title: Parse Windows Registry export files
user_story: As an analyst I want a .reg export turned into keys and typed values so I can inspect a captured registry snapshot.
expected_behavior: A file whose first non-blank content is "Windows Registry Editor Version 5.00" or "REGEDIT4" selects the Registry selection, and parse_registry_content returns keys with their values and value kinds (String, Dword, Qword, Binary with multi-line hex continuation, ExpandString, MultiString joined with " | ", None, DeleteMarker) plus totalKeys, totalValues, parseErrors, filePath and fileSize; UTF-16LE payloads inside a value are decoded and a long binary value is displayed truncated to its first 128 bytes with the total byte count appended. "@=" empty value names, escaped \\ and \" sequences, "-" delete markers and an empty file (zero keys, zero errors) are all handled.
entry_points: IPC parse_registry_file; registry viewer tab
notes: Extends LOG-024 (registry snapshot tab) with the parse contract; the registry parser is reached through parse_registry_file, not the log pipeline.

title: Parse .cmtlog files with sections, iterations and whatif markers
user_story: As an analyst I want exported CMTrace Open logs to reopen with their section structure and simulation flags intact.
expected_behavior: A .cmtlog extension selects the CmtLog parser immediately and content with __HEADER__/__SECTION__/__ITERATION__ components selects it heuristically when CCM lines are also present; reserved components mark entryKind Header/Section/Iteration, a Section sets the current section name and colour that later ordinary lines inherit, and the extended attributes section, color, tag, whatif and iteration are lifted onto the entry (whatif="1" becomes true, tag is split on commas). Extra key="value" attributes after file="" are tolerated by the relaxed regex, and lines that do not match are kept as plain text counted as errors.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on a .cmtlog file
notes: Extends LOG-012/LOG-013 (section banners, WhatIf styling) with the parse contract that produces those fields.

title: Parse PSADT Legacy deploy logs
user_story: As an analyst I want PSAppDeployToolkit Legacy lines split into timestamp, section, function and severity.
expected_behavior: Lines shaped [yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.fff] [Section] [Function] [Severity] :: message select the PsadtLegacy parser once two match; component is the section, sourceFile is the PSADT function, [Error]/[Warning]/[Warn]/[Success] map to Error/Warning/Warning/Success and anything else (including [Info]) to Info, and the display timestamp is MM-dd-yyyy HH:mm:ss.fff. A non-matching line (including a banner) is kept as a Plain entry with keyword severity.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on Deploy-Application.log
notes: Known sections: Initialization, Pre-Install, Install, Post-Install, Finalization.

title: Parse IIS W3C extended logs from their #Fields header
user_story: As an analyst I want IIS logs mapped regardless of which columns the server logged.
expected_behavior: A #Software: Microsoft Internet Information Services header on one of the first five lines, or an inetpub/logs or w3svc path hint with one data row (three rows without the hint), selects the IisW3c selection; the #Fields line defines the column names used to pick out date, time, cs-method, cs-uri-stem, cs-uri-query, sc-status, sc-substatus, time-taken, c-ip, s-ip, cs(User-Agent), s-port, cs-username and sc-win32-status, and the message is composed as "METHOD uri → status". 4xx maps to Warning and 5xx to Error, "-" fields become null instead of empty strings, '+' in the user agent is decoded as a space, and a data row shorter than the field list or an unusable row is kept as a fallback entry counted in parseErrors.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on an IIS W3C log
notes: Timestamps are read as UTC because W3C rows carry no offset.

title: Parse Windows DHCP server CSV logs
user_story: As an analyst I want DHCP lease logs to show the client, address and event meaning.
expected_behavior: A file starting with the Microsoft DHCP/DHCPv6 service-activity header, or a dhcpsrvlog/dhcpv6srvlog/dhcp_logs path hint with one CSV row (three rows without the hint), selects the Dhcp selection; the ~35-line header block is skipped, each CSV row becomes an entry whose message is "<eventid> - <description>" with ipAddress, hostName and MAC formatted as AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF, and event ids 14/15/31/34/35 are Error while 13/17/33/36 are Warning. A malformed row is kept as a Plain entry and counted in parseErrors.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on DhcpSrvLog-Mon.log
notes: Selection date order is MonthFirst (MM/DD/YY rows).

title: Parse DNS debug log PACKET records
user_story: As an analyst I want DNS server debug logs to show direction, query and response code per packet.
expected_behavior: A dns path hint plus one PACKET line (two without the hint) selects the DnsDebug selection (dedicated, Structured, LogicalRecord); a PACKET line starts a record and following non-PACKET lines are appended to it as detail text, with a "Remote addr X, port N" line appended to sourceIp as addr:port. Header lines before the first PACKET are skipped, protocol, direction, transaction id, flags and RCODE (with its severity: NXDOMAIN Warning, SERVFAIL/REFUSED/FORMERR Error, else Warning) are exposed, and a line containing PACKET that does not match the grammar increments parseErrors.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on dns.log
notes: DNS path hints widen the detection sample window from 20 to 50 lines so the ~29-line header is passed; dns_audit EVTX routing is a separate slice.

title: Decode DNS query names, types and response codes
user_story: As an analyst I want wire-format DNS names turned into readable names so that packets are searchable by host name.
expected_behavior: decode_query_name turns wire-format labels ((3)www(6)google(3)com(0)) and compression pointers ([C00C]) into a dotted name, treating (0) alone as ".", a dotted name keeps its labels with surrounding dots stripped, and a label length that lands mid-character stops decoding instead of slicing a Unicode payload. qtype_name and rcode_name map known codes to canonical names and fall back to UNKNOWN(n) / RCODE(n) for anything else.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on dns.log; query name/type/response code columns
notes: Mid-character label lengths are the issue #413 regression for wire names.

title: Parse macOS Intune MDM daemon logs
user_story: As a Mac admin I want pipe-delimited Intune daemon logs split into process, severity, thread and sub-component.
expected_behavior: Lines shaped YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS:mmm | Process | Severity | ThreadID | SubComponent | Message select the IntuneMacOs parser (dedicated, Structured, PhysicalLine); component is the process name (for example IntuneMDM-Daemon), sourceFile is the sub-component (for example SyncActivityTracer), the thread is the numeric thread id with its 0x display and E/W map to Error/Warning with everything else Info. A non-matching line (a continuation or JSON dump) is kept as a Plain entry counted in parseErrors.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on IntuneMDMDaemon.log
notes: Selection needs the intunemdmdaemon or /logs/microsoft/intune/ path hint with one record, or two records without the hint; the stamp carries no offset and is read as UTC.

title: Frame Intune Device Inventory logs by dialect
user_story: As an Intune engineer I want inventory logs read with the right dialect so that continuations stay attached to their record.
expected_behavior: Detection resolves the Device Inventory dialect from the file (Harvester, InventoryAdaptor or RotationFailure), which selects the IntuneDeviceInventory kind carrying that specialization, MonthFirst dates and LogicalRecord framing; a non-header line is attached to the record above it rather than emitted as a detached record, and the interface reports the dialect so the UI does not present a guess as validated.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on IntuneInventoryHarvesterLog.log / InventoryAdaptor.log
notes: LogicalRecord framing is required because the parser attaches continuations to the previous record in every dialect.

title: Degrade a Device Inventory selection without a dialect instead of panicking
user_story: As a maintainer I want a malformed selection to parse rather than abort the whole file.
expected_behavior: If an IntuneDeviceInventory selection arrives without a specialization (only possible from a hand-built selection or a future override surface) the parse falls back to the generic timestamped reading for that file instead of panicking, because all three dialects are timestamp-led and still produce usable records.
entry_points: parse_content_with_selection / parse_lines_with_selection callers (tailing, overrides)
notes: Deliberate degradation path; the guard exists in both the content and the line entry points.
error_detail: static-only: no dedicated test; the guard is a match arm in parser/mod.rs::parse_lines_with_selection and parse_content_with_selection

title: Specialise Intune agent logs as IME reads
user_story: As an Intune engineer I want AgentExecutor/AppWorkload style logs read as IME logical records so that script bodies stay on one row.
expected_behavior: When the file name starts with a known Intune agent prefix (agentexecutor, appactionprocessor, appworkload, clienthealth, healthscripts, intunemanagementextension) and the content carries CCM records, the selection is CCM with specialization Ime, framing LogicalRecord and Dedicated provenance; the prefix alone is not enough — a known IME file name whose content is not CCM is not specialised, and an IME-format CCM log living inside a Company Portal LocalState folder still selects CCM rather than Company Portal.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on HealthScripts.log / AppWorkload.log
notes: IME parsing itself lives in the Intune slice; this row is the detection/specialisation contract.

title: Detect Company Portal logs and downgrade an unvalidated app version
user_story: As an Intune engineer I want to know when a Company Portal log was read with a grammar that was not validated for its app version.
expected_behavior: A Company Portal file-name or package-folder hint plus one layout-matching record (two records without the hint) selects the CompanyPortal parser; when every matching record's app version is inside the validated set the provenance is Dedicated, and when any version is outside it the selection is marked Heuristic so the UI reports an unvalidated read even though the same grammar is still used. The exact LocalState file name with records from an unrelated UWP package, or generic timestamped content in a Company Portal path, is not claimed as Company Portal.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on LocalState Log_1.log; status bar parser segment
notes: Parse quality stays Structured; only provenance changes, so the reader is told without the parse being degraded.

title: Require corroborating records before trusting a path hint
user_story: As an analyst I want path hints to nominate rather than decide so that an unrelated file in a known folder is not misparsed.
expected_behavior: Dedicated detectors that are content-weighted require two matching records when no path hint is present (MSI, Burn, PatchMyPC, DNS debug, Intune macOS, Company Portal, IIS W3C, DHCP) and dedicated formats that are path-hint gated require at least one record inside the hinted path (CBS, DISM, Panther, ReportingEvents, SecureBoot); a single timestamp-looking line inside a 20-line sample is not enough to leave Plain, and a file that only shares a folder name with a format keeps its generic timestamped reading.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file on a log in an ambiguous folder
notes: This is the confidence rule behind the provenance/quality metadata; the thresholds are visible in detect_parser's decision ladder.

title: Rebuild one entry from a single raw line with a known parser
user_story: As a consumer of the parser API I want to materialise one line on demand so that on-demand views do not re-parse the whole file.
expected_behavior: ResolvedParser::parse_one_line strips one trailing newline, parses the single line with the already-resolved parser, overrides lineNumber with the caller's original line number and returns the entry; a line the parser produces nothing for returns an error string ("parser produced no entries") rather than a fabricated entry.
entry_points: parser API used by on-demand views (unified timeline materialisation, tail)
notes: Pure API helper; no IPC command of its own.
error_detail: static-only: no dedicated test; behaviour is exercised through src-tauri/src/watcher/tail.rs and unified-timeline materialisation call sites

title: Route a selection to its parser implementation and annotate error spans
user_story: As a caller I want one entry point to dispatch every parser and annotate codes so that downstream views are uniform.
expected_behavior: parse_lines_with_selection dispatches on the implementation, routes GenericTimestamped to the CBS, DISM or Panther parser when that ParserKind was detected (otherwise the generic timestamped parser), routes CCM to its specialisation-aware parser, and returns no line entries for Registry and DnsAudit because those take dedicated binary/IPC paths; after parsing, error-code spans are detected on every entry's message so a caller cannot forget the annotation. totalLines counts the content's lines and parseErrors is the parser's own count.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file / tail reads through parse_lines_with_selection and parse_content_with_selection
notes: Registry parses through parse_registry_file and DNS audit EVTX through the event-log binary path.

title: Detect supported error codes inside a message
user_story: As an analyst I want recognised error codes underlined in the message so that I can open their description.
expected_behavior: detect_error_code_spans finds 0x-prefixed 8-hex-digit tokens, skips a match followed by more hex digits (so GUIDs and longer hex runs are not split), and returns a span only for codes that exist in the database; each span carries codeHex, codeDecimal, description, category and outcome, and start/end are UTF-16 code-unit offsets so JavaScript string slicing lines up even when the message contains non-ASCII or emoji before the code. A message with no "0x"/"0X" returns no spans without running the regex.
entry_points: IPC open_log_file (spans on parsed entries); click a highlighted code in a message
notes: Extends LOG-008 (clicking an error code) with the backend span contract that makes the span clickable.

title: Look up an error code in any written form
user_story: As an analyst I want to paste a code however it was written and still get its description.
expected_behavior: lookup_error_code accepts 0x-prefixed hex, bare hex of six or more digits, negative decimal (the signed form of an HRESULT) and plain decimal, and returns codeHex, codeDecimal, description, category and found=true on a hit; an unknown but well-formed code returns found=false with the formatted values and description "Unknown error code", and unparseable input returns empty code fields with "Invalid error code format".
entry_points: IPC lookup_error_code; Tools > Error Code Lookup
notes: Extends CHROME-016 (the dialog) with the backend lookup contract it calls.

title: Resolve an HRESULT to its Win32 twin and back
user_story: As an analyst I want 0x80070005 and 5 to resolve to the same explanation.
expected_behavior: A miss on a FACILITY_WIN32 code (0x8007xxxx) is retried with its low 16 bits as a Win32 code, and a small value (0xFFFF or less) is retried as 0x80070000 | code, so looking up either spelling of a code finds the entry stored under the other; the table does not have to hold both forms for the lookup to succeed.
entry_points: IPC lookup_error_code; IPC search_error_codes
notes: O(1) lookup over a prebuilt OnceLock HashMap of the embedded table.

title: Search error codes by number or description text
user_story: As an analyst I want to type a phrase and get matching codes so that I can find a code I only half remember.
expected_behavior: search_error_codes returns an empty list for an empty query; a query that parses as a code returns that single code (with found=false and "Unknown error code" when the code is absent from the table); otherwise it matches descriptions case-insensitively with description-prefix matches ranked above description-substring matches, which rank above category-label matches, sorts by that priority and truncates to 50 results.
entry_points: IPC search_error_codes; Tools > Error Code Lookup text search
notes: Extends CHROME-016 with the search backend contract.

title: Attribute a code to its product category and triage outcome
user_story: As an analyst I want a code's category and whether it really is a failure so that success codes are not counted as findings.
expected_behavior: Each entry carries a label from ErrorCategory (Windows, Windows Update, BITS, ConfigMgr, Intune, Delivery Optimization, App Install, Certificate, Network, Security, Registry, File System, Windows Installer (MSI), PSADT) and a lookup result reports it, for example 0x87D13B64 as Intune and the published 0x87D0xxxx Configuration Manager codes as ConfigMgr. error_code_outcome classifies 0x00000000/0x00000001 and the WU_S_* codes as Success, 3010/0x80070BC2/0x00240005 as SuccessRequiresAction and 1641 and 0x87D1076C as Success, while everything else (including MSI 1707/1724/1726/1728, which other code spaces reuse) stays Failure so findings are not under-counted; a code inside a published range but not published (0x87D01282) fails closed as unknown.
entry_points: IPC lookup_error_code / search_error_codes; error-code table that counts findings
notes: The table is also asserted to hold no duplicate codes and to contain every code classified as non-failure (codes_outside_failure_exist_in_the_table, test_no_duplicate_error_codes, test_expanded_database_size).

title: Render an event description from captured provider metadata
user_story: As an analyst opening someone else's EVTX I want event descriptions rendered without the provider being installed.
expected_behavior: render_description substitutes %1/%2/… (one-based, %10 selecting the tenth value) with the event's insertion strings, treats %% as a literal percent and passes any other % through untouched; insertions the event did not supply stay visible as %n and are listed in missingInsertions so a partial render cannot be mistaken for a complete one, and RenderedDescription::is_complete reports that state. ProviderMetadata::render_event_description produces the same result on any platform without consulting a Windows registry.
entry_points: Event description text in the Event Viewer detail pane (via the host layer that reads captured metadata)
notes: Complements EVTX-010 (provider map/enrichment): this row is the pure rendering half, which works identically on macOS/Linux/wasm.

title: Pick the right provider event definition
user_story: As an analyst I want the description that matches the event's version and channel so that insertion points line up.
expected_behavior: ProviderMetadata::event prefers an event definition whose version matches exactly and whose channel matches the event's channel; when no exact version exists it falls back to the highest known version, and a channel-specific definition beats a wildcard definition at the same version. An unknown event id resolves to no definition (and therefore no rendered description) rather than a guess from a sibling channel.
entry_points: Event description text in the Event Viewer detail pane
notes: Channel tiering deliberately precedes the version fallback so a plausible-but-wrong description is not rendered.

title: Name provider levels, tasks, opcodes and keyword bits
user_story: As an analyst I want keyword bitmasks expanded to names so that filtering by keyword is meaningful.
expected_behavior: ProviderMetadata resolves a task value and an opcode value through the provider's tables, and keyword_names expands a mask into the declared names of the set bits only (undeclared bits, including the reserved high bits the system sets, are ignored rather than reported as unknown) returned in bit-value order instead of the map's lexicographic key order. An absent category is recorded in unavailableCategories so it stays distinguishable from a present-but-empty one, and source_os_build records which Windows build the metadata came from.
entry_points: Event keyword/task/opcode display in the Event Viewer detail pane
notes: Ordering is by bit value because string-ordered keys ("1", "16", "2") read as meaningful when they are an artefact.

title: Tolerate the signed wire form of provider metadata
user_story: As an analyst I want providers whose masks or message ids use the top bit to load instead of failing silently.
expected_behavior: Keyword masks and short message ids written as signed .NET integers deserialize into the unsigned model (a mask of -9223372036854775808 becomes 0x8000000000000000) and serialize back in the signed form so metadata round-trips; a ShortId outside the signed Int16 range, or an in-memory value wider than a 16-bit low word, is rejected with an error rather than truncated.
entry_points: Loading captured provider metadata into the app
notes: Without the signed handling the Microsoft-Windows-DeviceManagement provider failed to load at all.

title: Read WIM metadata from a raw image without decompressing
user_story: As an engineer I want the image list of a .wim read without wimlib so that image metadata can be inspected portably.
expected_behavior: parse_wim validates the MSWIM magic and the 208-byte header size, decodes the header flags into a compression algorithm (None, Xpress, Lzx, Lzms or Unknown), slices the resources with explicit bounds checks, decodes the UTF-16LE XML resource and returns each image's index, name, dirCount, fileCount and totalBytes together with the raw XML, version, guid, chunk size, part numbers and boot index. The header's declared image count must equal the number of <IMAGE> elements or the parse fails.
entry_points: Library API used for WIM/ESD image metadata (no IPC command yet)
notes: Layer 1 only: pure byte-slice parsing, no decompression and no filesystem I/O; the module is only consumed by the crate's tests today.

title: Report unsupported WIM capabilities as coverage states
user_story: As an engineer I want an unsupported image reported as unsupported rather than returned as a half-read success.
expected_behavior: TooSmall, BadMagic, BadHeader, ResourceOutOfBounds, UnsupportedCompression, InvalidUtf16, MalformedXml{reason}, ImageCountMismatch, SpannedUnsupported and UnsupportedVersion are distinct errors: a spanned (.swm) set, a compressed XML resource, a header version other than 0x10D00, a declared header size mismatch, an odd-length UTF-16 XML resource and a non-XML document root each fail with their own variant, so a caller can tell a coverage gap from a parse failure.
entry_points: Library API used for WIM/ESD image metadata
notes: UnsupportedVersion is intentionally a coverage state, not a generic failure.

title: Report an unavailable evidence source as a coverage gap
user_story: As an analyst I want missing evidence called out as missing so that a quiet report is not read as a healthy machine.
expected_behavior: finding_for_coverage builds a CoverageGap class finding for one of Covered/Unknown/Absent/AccessDenied/Capped/Skipped/Unsupported/Malformed/ParseFailed/ProviderDescriptionUnavailable with a deterministic id, the source name, the detail text and a recommended check to collect or grant access to that source, at Info severity and Unknown confidence, and carries the gap itself in the finding's coverageGaps so the incompleteness travels with the conclusion.
entry_points: Diagnosis summaries shown by the Intune/ESP/SCCM workspaces and the unified timeline
notes: Coverage is deliberately modelled separately from an assertion about a source's health.

title: Enrich error tokens in a message losslessly
user_story: As an analyst I want every code-looking token explained without losing how it was written.
expected_behavior: enrich_error_tokens returns the known spans found by the shared detector first and then adds wider candidates (0x-prefixed, signed, four-or-more-digit numerics and bare 8-hex tokens), where a bare numeric token is only taken when the surrounding sentence contains a context marker such as error, hresult, code, status, failed or failure. Each ErrorToken keeps the original spelling in raw plus parsed decimal/hex, a malformed flag for unparseable input, and found/description/category only when the database resolved it; duplicate spellings are emitted once.
entry_points: Diagnosis event views (error tokens list)
notes: Lossless by design: an unknown or malformed token is still reported rather than dropped.

entry_points: Diagnosis summary export and cross-source overview in the workspaces

title: Start live diagnostics and follow it out of Starting
user_story: As a Windows admin I want one click to begin collecting live ESP evidence so that the cockpit fills in without further setup.
expected_behavior: Start live diagnostics creates a fresh UUID request id, calls start_esp_diagnostics_session, applies the returned envelope as an initialSnapshot update and, while the state is still starting, polls get_esp_diagnostics_session every 100 ms until the session leaves starting or this request/session no longer owns the Starting state; the control then becomes Stop live diagnostics. The button is disabled off Windows and while analyzing/starting/stopping, a failed start shows the error alert, and no session is ever resumed that the workspace does not own.
entry_points: ESP workspace > Start live diagnostics (Play icon); empty-state copy 'Live acquisition requires Windows.' / 'Windows live acquisition is read-only.'
notes: Extends ESP-003 with the starting-owner poll and the ownership rule; session updates also arrive on the esp-diagnostics-session-update event and are dropped unless isEspSessionUpdate passes.
test_method: component_test: polls a starting session until live when the initial event was missed

title: Reject invalid or duplicate live session starts
user_story: As an integration caller I want typed start failures so that I can tell a bad request from an already-running session.
expected_behavior: start_esp_diagnostics_session returns 'ESP diagnostics request ID must be a UUID' for a non-UUID request id, 'live ESP diagnostics are only supported on Windows' when live support is absent, and 'an ESP diagnostics session is already active: <existing id>' while a session is running; the successful envelope carries sessionId, requestId, sequence 0, state starting and the initial snapshot, and a worker that cannot be spawned yields the worker error after clearing the reservation.
entry_points: IPC start_esp_diagnostics_session
notes: Companion get_esp_diagnostics_session rejects a non-UUID session id and returns 'ESP diagnostics session was not found' for an unknown or superseded one.

title: Keep one live owner with debounced, monotonic updates
user_story: As an admin I want one live collection that updates steadily so that the cockpit never flickers or goes backwards.
expected_behavior: A single session owns acquisition; evidence changes are debounced by 250 ms, discovery refreshes every 2 s while live, and every esp-diagnostics-session-update carries a strictly increasing sequence so an older or duplicate sequence is ignored by the store. A refresh that partially loses sources keeps those partial coverage entries instead of clearing them, and tail-only updates use the post-poll UTC time without disturbing the monotonic debounce.
entry_points: esp-diagnostics-session-update event; workspace live phase
notes: The frontend additionally rejects a same-session update from a different request id and accepts sequence 0 exactly once as the initial update.
test_method: component_test: accepts sequence zero exactly once as the initial live update

title: Stop live diagnostics

title: Discover bounded ESP-phase log sources
user_story: As a support engineer I want live collection to find the ESP-phase logs without scanning the whole disk so that acquisition stays fast and predictable.
expected_behavior: The candidate set comes from the embedded collection families (intune-ime, configmgr, msi, panther, setup, windows-update, wpm) plus the curated Windows deployment sources; per stem only the current file and at most three newest rotations are kept, temp roots are the four fixed categories scanned non-recursively with at most the 128 newest entries inspected and a 30-minute lookback, entry probing is capped at 512 per root and 4096 per temp root, and there is no arbitrary-root or deep-scan mode reachable from IPC.

title: Report unreadable or unsafe log paths as coverage

", "... rejected symlink entry"), the failure list is capped at 256 with truncation flagged, and candidates that are symlinks, reparse points, or resolve outside an allowed root are rejected with a typed containment failure before any read.

title: Tail ESP-phase logs with bounded reads and reset detection
user_story: As an admin I want live logs tailed safely so that an actively written installer log is followed without unbounded memory or missed restarts.
expected_behavior: Each source is attached once with priority current IME then active installer log then rotations then temp logs, under a 16-active-tail cap with deterministic eviction of a lower-priority tail and a bounded dormant-cursor cache where reattachment is an explicit Reattached reset; each poll compares the 64-byte consumed anchor so an in-place copytruncate is detected alongside Truncated and Rotated; the first attachment reads at most the final 8 MiB, an unterminated record is bounded to 8 MiB instead of being emitted, missing/denied/replaced files raise typed failures, and Windows opens request read/write/delete sharing.
entry_points: Live session tail polling; live evidence dock rows
notes: Tail session cap MAX_SESSION_TAIL_SOURCES is 512; failed higher-priority attachments do not consume the budget of an existing entry.
