user_story: As an admin I want the evidence panel cheap until I open it and I want Graph names beside raw ids, not instead of them.
expected_behavior: A family's item bodies are not mounted until its disclosure is opened ('Collapsible source detail - read-only' header) while the summary always shows the family name, description, state and item count; an item keeps 'Raw ID - <rawIdentifier>' visible and an available Graph name is added as a separate 'Microsoft Graph - <name>' line, so the raw identifier is never replaced by a friendly name.
entry_points: ESP workspace > ESP evidence family summary toggle
notes: Extends ESP-013/ESP-010; Graph names are only ever additive in evidence, workloads and findings.
test_method: component_test: does not mount evidence item bodies until their disclosure is opened

title: Show Graph enrichment availability and control refresh/cancel
user_story: As an admin I want to know whether Graph enrichment is off, unavailable or unconnected so that I never wait on a query that cannot run.
expected_behavior: The panel header reads 'Optional - existing WAM connection - read-only' and one of 'Graph enrichment is off' (Graph disabled), 'Graph unavailable on this platform', 'GraphNotConnected' with 'Connect in Settings -> Graph API, then return here and refresh explicitly. This workspace never opens Windows sign-in or queues a request behind it.', 'Ready for explicit refresh', 'Graph query in progress', 'Enrichment complete', 'Partial enrichment', 'Graph query failed' (with the error text) or 'Graph query cancelled'; 'Refresh Graph data' is disabled unless connected and not loading, 'Cancel Graph query' appears only while loading, and a synchronous control failure (Cancel or device selection) is contained in a role=alert line under the state copy instead of breaking the panel.
entry_points: ESP workspace > Microsoft Graph enrichment panel
notes: Extends ESP-010 with the exact state copy and the control-level error containment.
test_method: component_test: keeps disabled and connecting states local-only and requires an explicit refresh after connection

title: Show independent Graph section status, scope, and error detail
user_story: As an admin I want each Graph section to fail on its own terms so that one denial does not blank the rest of the enrichment.
expected_behavior: Each section card (Managed device, Autopilot identity, Deployment profile, Intended deployment profile, Profile assignments, Autopilot events, Enrollment Status Page configuration, Applications, Policies, Scripts) shows the requested scope or 'No additional scope requested', the API version ('Beta' badge for beta, the version for v1, 'Not requested' for notRequested), and a status label/icon/colour for Available / Not found / Permission denied / Failed / Skipped / Cancelled / 'Unknown - <status>'; on error it shows '<code> - <message>' plus ' - Blocked by <section>' and ' - Retry after <N> seconds' when present, and assignment lines render 'Declared targeting - <Intent> - <targetKind> - <targetId|target unavailable>' with the filter id when set.
entry_points: ESP workspace > Microsoft Graph enrichment section cards
notes: Extends ESP-010.
test_method: component_test: shows independent partial, denied, offline, throttled, cancelled, and beta section states

title: Require explicit device selection when Graph matching is ambiguous
user_story: As an admin I want to pick the right managed device when the match is ambiguous so that enrichment cannot silently describe the wrong device.
expected_behavior: With candidates but no selection the Managed device card shows 'Selection is required before dependent queries can continue' and one button per candidate labelled 'Select Graph device <managedDeviceId>' with 'Use device' (disabled while disconnected or loading); choosing one re-queries Graph with that managedDeviceId through the coordinator request, and the selected match then displays the device name, its id, and 'Match basis - <basis> - <Confidence> confidence'; a notFound match shows 'No managed device match' and a rejected explicit selection never falls back to local identity.
entry_points: ESP workspace > Microsoft Graph enrichment > Managed device card
notes: Extends ESP-010; the explicit selection is normalized to a GUID before it enters the request.
test_method: component_test: requires explicit selection for ambiguous managed-device candidates

title: Reject invalid Graph overlays and keep local evidence authoritative
user_story: As an admin I want a failed or unexpected Graph response to leave my local evidence untouched so that enrichment can never corrupt a diagnosis.
expected_behavior: An overlay failing isEspGraphOverlay, one whose requestId differs from the issued request, or a transport failure leaves local findings, workloads and raw ids intact while setting graphPhase error and showing 'Graph enrichment failed. Local evidence remains available; check the Graph connection and retry.'; a replayed capture never triggers a fetch, disabling Graph or losing the connection clears the overlay via setGraphUnavailable('graphDisabled'|'graphNotConnected'), and an identity change while a request is in flight invalidates it so the late overlay is discarded and the next local run restarts enrichment.
entry_points: ESP workspace > Graph enrichment error alert; Graph pill in header/status bar
notes: Extends ESP-010 with the malformed-data, mismatched-request, identity-change and offline-clearing paths.
test_method: component_test: keeps local IDs and evidence visible after a remote query error

title: Orchestrate ESP Graph reads with dependency skips, isolated denials, and bounded requests
user_story: As an Intune engineer I want Graph reads that degrade per section and stop on demand so that enrichment never stalls a live session.
expected_behavior: With no selected device every dependent section becomes skipped with blockedBy 'deviceMatch'; a permission denial or malformed success fails only its own section with a sanitized error while sibling sections keep their data; cancellation marks the affected section and its dependents Cancelled (the device section cancels all dependents); beta is used only to fill fields v1 lacks (a beta enrollment failure keeps the v1 configuration); referenced-object and page caps mark sections partial; the IPC layer refuses a fetch when Graph is not connected ('GraphNotConnected'), rejects invalid/duplicate/over-limit request ids ('InvalidGraphRequestId', 'GraphRequestAlreadyActive', 'GraphRequestLimitReached'), bounds concurrent operations to 32 with a 120-second overall deadline, cancels only the exact owned request id (equivalently-spelled UUIDs share one owner), and returns typed PlatformUnsupported 'GraphEspDiagnostics' for fetch and cancel off Windows.
entry_points: IPC graph_fetch_esp_diagnostics / graph_cancel_esp_diagnostics
notes: Extends ESP-010 from the backend side; no interactive sign-in is ever opened by this path.

title: Export a redacted ESP session capture
user_story: As an admin I want to hand a session to support as a single file so that they can replay it without device access.
expected_behavior: 'Export session' is disabled until a snapshot exists, asks for a destination defaulting to esp-session-<timestamp>.json with the 'ESP session capture' filter, and calls export_esp_session with the displayed snapshot plus capturedAtUtc; the backend builds an EspSessionCapture (the frontend never serializes a snapshot) and writes it to a sibling '<dest>.<pid>.<nanos>.tmp' file renamed into place, removing the temp on failure so an existing capture is never truncated; serialize/write failures surface as 'the ESP session capture could not be serialized: <message>' / 'the ESP session capture could not be written: <message>' and the workspace reports 'Could not export the ESP session: <message>'.
entry_points: ESP workspace > Export session; IPC export_esp_session
notes: Extends ESP-002; the atomic temp-write/rename path has no automated test (static review only).
test_method: component_test: never writes a cleartext session through the generic file writer

title: Validate a session capture file before opening it
user_story: As a support engineer I want clear rejections for unreadable captures so that a schema drift is obvious.
expected_behavior: Opening a .json runs parseEspSessionCapture: a capture envelope's snapshot is revalidated with the same wire guard as live updates; a version above 1 is rejected with 'This capture is version <N>, newer than this build understands (1). Update CMTrace Open to open it.', a malformed snapshot with "This capture's snapshot is malformed or from an incompatible schema.", invalid JSON with 'That file is not valid JSON.', anything else with 'That file is not an ESP session capture or diagnostics snapshot.', and an unreadable file with 'Could not read <path>: <error>'; a bare snapshot without an envelope loads as a replay, and a .json that fails capture parsing is retried as a bundle by the importer.
entry_points: ESP workspace > Open session; Import captured evidence with a .json
notes: Extends ESP-002 with the four rejection messages and the bare-snapshot acceptance.

title: Render a replayed capture as captured and inert
user_story: As a support engineer I want a replayed session clearly marked as captured and unable to touch my machine so that I cannot confuse it with a live device.
expected_behavior: loadReplaySession marks the session as a replay, drives the Graph pill straight from the captured overlay (ready; partial when any section or app intent state is not available/notFound/skipped; disabled with reason graphDisabled when the capture carries no overlay), and clears unread and boundary-marker state; the current-task block labels the source 'Captured' rather than 'Live', the 'Force past ESP' actions are absent because the write actions only target a live local session, and the captured snapshot stays fully browsable and exportable.
entry_points: ESP workspace after Open session / importing a session capture
notes: Extends ESP-002 with the replay rendering contract.
test_method: component_test: loadReplaySession marks the session inert and drives the Graph pill from the overlay

title: Gate the Force past ESP action by platform, replay, and elevation
user_story: As an elevated Windows admin I want the write action to appear only when it applies so that I cannot run it against a capture or an unsupported platform.
expected_behavior: The Actions panel renders only for a Windows, non-replayed session with at least one failed Win32 app in the latest session (the 'Actions' nav pill appears and disappears with it) and is absent when there are none; while not elevated it shows 'Run CMTrace Open as administrator to use these actions (writing to HKLM requires elevation).' and 'Force past ESP' is disabled; each row shows the app name (display name, else Graph name, else raw identifier) with the enforcement-error or exit-code hex, falling back to 'Failed'.
entry_points: ESP workspace > Actions panel ('Force ESP past a failed app')
notes: Extends ESP-007 with the elevation message, the hidden-state rules and the row labelling.
test_method: component_test: renders nothing when there are no failed apps

title: Confirm and force a failed app past the ESP
user_story: As an elevated admin I want an explicit confirmation and an undo before I change this device's registry so that I can unblock ESP safely.
expected_behavior: 'Force past ESP' opens 'Force ESP past this app?' naming 'this device's' registry and the app, listing that it sets InstallationState to Installed (3), clears the recorded error and backs up first, and warning that the app is not installed by this; confirming calls esp_flip_app_installed and the row then shows 'Forced to Installed. Click Try again on the ESP; the app is still not installed.' with a 'Restore' button (spinner while pending) that calls esp_restore_app_state with the returned backup and clears the outcome; a flip or restore failure prints the error text in the row, and the confirmation dialog yields ownership to any app modal in front of it and releases it on unmount.
entry_points: ESP workspace > Actions > Force past ESP > 'Force past ESP' in the dialog; row 'Restore'
notes: Extends ESP-007 with the dialog content, the success copy and the modal-ownership handoff.
test_method: component_test: flips a failed app after confirmation and then offers restore

title: Refuse unsafe app identifiers and unsupported platforms for ESP remediation
user_story: As a security reviewer I want the registry write to validate its target so that a crafted identifier cannot escape the Sidecar key.
expected_behavior: The flip and restore paths validate the app id as 1-256 characters of ASCII alphanumerics, '_' or '-' only, otherwise failing with 'Refusing to write an unexpected app identifier: "<id>"' (rejecting ', /, .., spaces, dotted segments and brace-wrapped GUIDs); off Windows they then return "Forcing an app's ESP state is only available on Windows." / "Restoring an app's ESP state is only available on Windows."; the flip returns appId, installationState 3 and a backup holding the previous InstallationState and ErrorHresult as Option (None meaning the value must be deleted on restore), and a missing or unelevated key yields 'Could not open the app's ESP tracking key (run elevated): <error>'.
entry_points: IPC esp_flip_app_installed / esp_restore_app_state
notes: The only device-mutating path in the ESP lane; a decorated id such as Win32App_<guid>_1 is accepted.

title: Redact classified fields and their literals on export
user_story: As a privacy-conscious admin I want exported captures to be scrubbed by construction so that sharing a session cannot leak local identifiers.
expected_behavior: redacted_export_projection masks every classified field to '[redacted]', scrubs each masked value's literal (and case variants) out of every free-text field - narrative strings, coverage details, workload display names and statuses, registration messages and named data, activity titles/details, profile names, installer reasons and command lines, referenced log paths and provenance - and pseudonymizes SIDs consistently so a SID keeps a stable identity across the export; the caller's snapshot is untouched, the returned snapshot is reassembled field by field so a new field cannot ride out unexamined, and EspSessionCapture has no Deserialize or field-wise constructor so an unprojected capture cannot be assembled.
entry_points: IPC export_esp_session -> crates/cmtraceopen-parser EspSessionCapture::from_snapshot
notes: Envelope carries kind 'esp-session-capture', version 1, capturedAtUtc, app version/commit and redacted: true (always written, never inferred).

title: Scrub exact literals without mangling readable evidence
user_story: As a support engineer I want redaction to be precise so that the shared capture still reads as real evidence.
expected_behavior: Scrubbing combines shaped rules (emails, SIDs, MAC addresses, IPv4 and IPv6 including '::'-compressed, bracketed and IPv4-mapped forms, user-profile paths under Users/Documents and Settings, Bearer/Digest/Basic and unknown-scheme Authorization values, Azure Storage sig/skoid/SharedAccessSignature/AccountKey values) with literal values of at least 6 bytes taken from the fields being masked, so a degenerate firmware serial such as '0' or 'N/A' does not scrub unrelated narrative, a literal never removes a substring of a longer identifier, C++-style '::' tokens are not mistaken for addresses, and text exceeding 256 KiB is replaced by '[redacted: oversized text omitted]'.
entry_points: Export projection; reused as redact_text by other evidence modules
notes: The rule table is crate-internal (pub(crate) redact_text) so sibling evidence modules cannot drift from it.

title: Omit credential-bearing raw records and never retain hardware hashes
user_story: As a privacy-conscious admin I want credential-bearing or hardware-hash evidence dropped rather than masked so that a capture cannot carry a secret at all.
expected_behavior: On export, raw records whose source is graph, whose labels are secret-like (password/passwd/pwd/secret/clientSecret/apiKey/token/authorization/...token/hardwareHash/deviceHardwareData/rawGraphBody/graphResponseBody) or whose text matches a credential pattern (JSON secret members, Authorization headers, digest challenges, SAS parameters) are removed entirely; surviving sensitive/restricted or NodeCache-backed values are replaced with '[redacted]' and their record ids and provenance are redacted; independently, the reducer drops hardware-hash material (registry key/value names or JSON document type/pointer) at ingest so it never appears in raw evidence; and the MSIEXEC panel masks password/token/secret/api_key/authorization arguments and 'Bearer <token>' as '[REDACTED]' before display.
entry_points: Export projection; ESP evidence raw provenance; MSIEXEC 'What MSIEXEC is doing now' command line
notes: Covers both the export boundary and the UI-level display redaction; delivery-optimization transfer/content/app ids are also masked on export.

title: Redact secrets from installer and agent command lines
user_story: As an admin I want command lines safe to read and export so that troubleshooting never exposes credentials.
expected_behavior: Command lines are sanitized before storage: named secrets (password/passwd/pwd/secret/client_secret/api_key/token and related variants), Authorization headers (Bearer, Digest, Basic and unknown schemes, including one-layer escaped JSON), query-string secrets, JSON-embedded secret values, hardware-identity fields and standalone digest challenges are replaced, while safe sibling arguments, MSI log switch paths (/l*v <path>) and benign authentication narratives are preserved; ambiguous, unterminated or wider-quote secret shapes fail closed (over-redacted rather than leaked), and the MSIEXEC row shows the sanitized value or 'Command line unavailable' when none exists.
entry_points: Live process evidence; MSIEXEC status row command line; ESP evidence 'Raw provenance'
notes: Also applied to event-log command lines via contains_sensitive_identity_text/sanitize_command_line.

title: Show what the device is doing right now
user_story: As an admin I want a live 'now' readout so that I can see which workload is being processed without reading the table.
expected_behavior: The Action Center's live block derives the current task from the latest session's workloads: a running workload shows '<STATUS> <name>' plus ' +N more' when several run (the most recently started or updated wins), a completed phase shows 'COMPLETE - Enrollment complete', a failure shows 'FAILED - <app>', queued-only shows 'WAITING - Next of N queued workloads' or 'Waiting for next workload', and no workloads shows 'IDLE - Awaiting workload telemetry' (or 'No active workload' when workloads exist but none are active); the progress bar renders done/running/failed segments with '<done> / <total> complete' plus running/failed/queued counts, the pill reads 'Live' with a pulsing dot or 'Captured', and the aria-label announces 'Current task: <label>. <primary>. <done> of <total> workloads complete.'.
entry_points: ESP workspace > Action center top block
notes: Extends ESP-006 with every headline state and the count/progress semantics.
test_method: component_test: shows the actively installing workload as the live current task

title: Show the effective workload status and per-row details
user_story: As an admin I want the worst known state of a workload visible with the raw wire values so that a nested failure cannot hide behind a friendly outer status.
expected_behavior: A workload whose status.detail is more severe than its outer status displays the detail status as the effective state with that state's glyph and colour plus 'Outer - <display>' and 'Detail - <display>' lines, 'Raw - <raw>' and 'Detail raw - <raw>', and the scope/blocking text ('Blocking', 'Non-blocking' or 'Blocking unknown'); 'View full values' lazily reveals the workload id, session id, first-observed raw timestamp and linked evidence ids.
entry_points: ESP workspace > Tracked workloads table rows
notes: Extends ESP-009 with the nested-status severity rule and the per-row detail disclosure.
test_method: component_test: uses nested status detail for visual severity and shows both wire statuses

title: Report a failure with no identified stage
user_story: As an admin I want an unidentified failure stage stated as unknown so that the phase view cannot imply a stage the evidence does not support.
expected_behavior: When the snapshot phase is failed but no latest session names devicePreparation/deviceSetup/accountSetup, every step renders 'Unknown' with '?' and the footer reads 'Failure observed - Failing stage not identified in the collected evidence.' instead of guessing; the two step models stay distinct - 'Classic ESP phases' (Device preparation / Device setup / Account setup) with 'Classic ESP evaluates device and account setup as separate blocking phases.', and 'Device Preparation phases' (Agent bootstrap / Policy + scripts / Applications + certificates / Completion) with 'Device Preparation tracks agent, scripts, applications, and certificates under its own timeout and skip rules.' - and notStarted keeps every step Pending in both.
entry_points: ESP workspace > ESP phase progress
notes: Extends ESP-011 with the unknown-stage failure path and the footer copy.
test_method: component_test: does not invent a failing stage when the snapshot only reports failure

title: Acquire registry and event-log evidence within fixed bounds
user_story: As a support engineer I want native evidence reads bounded and their failures typed so that collection stays quick and gaps are explained.
expected_behavior: Registry reads use read-only access with the 64-bit view from the fixed ESP roots, enforce depth 8, 4096 keys, 16384 values, 64 KiB per value and 16 MiB total under a 3-second budget with at most 256 uninstall-name lookups, retain hive/key/value provenance, exclude hardware-hash keys/values and NodeCache hardware payloads before any evidence exists, and distinguish missing from permission-denied per root while keeping descendant failures when the root is available; event acquisition queries only the two ESP channels for the 14 required event ids before applying a 2000-record-per-channel cap, keeps ordered named properties and record ids, and yields identical output regardless of provider ordering.
entry_points: Live session acquisition pass; ESP evidence families 'Hardware', 'NodeCache', 'Join and registration'
platforms: windows (logic testable all with injected providers)

title: Sample installer processes within an allowlist
user_story: As an admin I want process sampling restricted and identity-safe so that the MSIEXEC correlation is trustworthy.
expected_behavior: Sampling queries only the fixed allowlist (IntuneManagementExtension.exe, AgentExecutor.exe, msiexec.exe, winget.exe) plus at most 32 de-duplicated registry-derived installer names, and a dynamically derived name is accepted only with trusted Intune ancestry so generic interpreters are never promoted; process identity is pid plus start time so PID reuse cannot merge samples, the parent chain binds to the instance that existed when the child started and is bounded to depth 16, a timed-out batch keeps bounded partial observations without treating untrusted snapshots as partial, and the live provider is explicitly unsupported off Windows.
entry_points: Live session process sampling; MSIEXEC status and evidence 'Raw provenance'
notes: Correlation itself lives in the parser crate (EspInstallerCorrelation) and is surfaced by ESP-008.

title: Open EVTX and diagnostic sources
user_story: As an admin I open one or more event-log sources without losing provenance or unread coverage.
expected_behavior: The Full-edition Event Log Viewer opens selected EVTX files, recursive folders, wildcard/archive/VSS selections, known sources, File-menu paths, and drag-dropped paths through one bounded manifest contract. Supported diagnostic ZIPs contribute EVTX and bounded text records; unsupported registry/binary members remain visible as hashed inventory. Source identity, archive-member outcomes, child traversal failures, and aggregate limits survive into the workspace. Every zero-entry manifest reports bounded diagnostics, including plural file selection, wildcard/archive/VSS paths, folders, and known sources while prior data remains visible.
entry_points: SourcePicker Open .evtx files / Open folder recursively; File > Open / Open Folder / Known Sources; drag-drop
notes: Focused frontend and portable Rust regressions cover every source route, recursive manifests, empty plural and special-source manifests, archive/member provenance, partial coverage, bounded diagnostics, and persistent loaded-state errors. Native file dialogs plus elevated Windows archived-log/VSS access remain platform acceptance; this lane does not claim a real Windows source run.
error_detail: The shipped cross-platform parse and diagnostic-ZIP paths have automated evidence, but native dialogs and Windows-only archived-log/VSS behavior were not exercised on this macOS lane.
fix_notes: The repaired source-open coordinator shares one generation and empty-manifest validator across direct, plural, folder, wildcard/archive/VSS, known, drag-drop, and channel-enumeration paths; stale completions are ignored while current failures remain visible.

ChannelPicker can load selected channels, refresh loaded channels, start/stop subscription-or-polling live tail, and request an elevated confirmed clear. Query, stream, stop, clear, access, and remote-session failures remain coverage gaps instead of empty success.

The actual wevtapi local/remote query, subscription, polling, credential, elevation, and clear behavior is Windows-only and has not run on this macOS lane.

The backend applies the common redaction/formula-safety projection, rejects a destination that would overwrite a loaded source, validates XML-bearing output, writes through an owner-only staged file, and atomically replaces the destination. The UI reports the exported count/KB or a bounded failure.

expected_behavior: Selecting a grid row opens a resizable detail pane with Event ID/time/level, rendered message, Event Data, provider/channel/computer/source/record identity, task/opcode/PID/TID/keywords/SID, explicit correlation identities, optional mapped fields, and Show/Hide Raw XML. Evidence: marker-store, evtx-marker, LogListView, and Event Viewer component tests.

title: Coverage and provenance banner
user_story: As a user I know what was not read or only inventoried.
expected_behavior: A non-dismissible live status region merges legacy source messages, structured parse gaps, and live-tail gaps without duplicates. It also exposes bounded archive-member provenance including member kind, parsed/unsupported/malformed/duplicate/limit outcome, and optional SHA-256. Coverage gaps display at most 256 entries and archive-member metadata at most 4096 entries with separate omitted counts; the operator may collapse details but cannot dismiss the coverage state while the source remains loaded.

notes: Component and decoder tests cover deduplication, structured gap formatting, archive-member decisions, collision-free keys, the 256/4096 display bounds, separate omitted summaries, and live-region behavior. Native gap producers remain bounded by their source stories EVTX-001/EVTX-002.
error_detail: No confirmed defect in the coverage/provenance presentation contract.

title: Event Viewer server query filters
user_story: As an administrator I want exact live predicates applied before records reach the list without silently changing local semantics.
expected_behavior: For live channels the store sends time-window predicates, valid Event ID singles/ranges in include mode, and selected levels when the set excludes Information. Information retains provider-defined raw levels 6-254, so any selection containing it stays local rather than issuing an incomplete XPath. Invalid Event ID input requests zero records and remains visibly invalid locally. Search, quick filters, hide mode, case sensitivity, visible-column scope, grouping, and provider text remain local because no exact shipped server equivalent exists. title: Append or replace timeline sources without interleaving
user_story: As an analyst I want adding files to add to the timeline, and New Timeline to start clean.
expected_behavior: area=timeline; openTimelineSource appends: it takes the file path, or a folder's non-directory children - plus the folder path itself when AgentExecutor.log or IntuneManagementExtension.log is present - and rebuilds the timeline from the deduplicated union with the existing bundle's sources. An empty path list is a no-op. replaceTimelineSource clears the current bundle first and builds from the new selection only. All opens run through one serialised queue that records any failure via setLoadError, and a build that finishes after a newer open started does not publish its bundle.
entry_points: File > Open / drag-drop with the Timeline workspace active
notes: Extends TL-001 with the queue, the empty-replacement and stale-build rules.
test_method: component_test: serializes overlapping opens so later files are not lost

title: New Timeline menu actions
user_story: As an analyst I want menu-driven folder timelines and a way to start over.
expected_behavior: area=timeline; File > New Timeline from Folder… opens a directory picker, makes the Timeline workspace visible and calls replaceTimelineSource for the chosen folder. File > New Timeline > Empty Timeline clears the bundle (setBundle(null)) and shows the Timeline workspace; a build that was already running when the empty timeline was requested does not restore a bundle afterwards.
entry_points: File > New Timeline > "New Timeline from Folder…"; File > New Timeline > "Empty Timeline"
notes: Extends TL-001 (menu ids file.new_timeline_from_folder, file.new_empty_timeline).
test_method: component_test: does not restore a build completed after New Timeline Empty

title: Timeline store state transitions and cache bounds
user_story: As an analyst I want switching timelines or filters never to leave stale lane or row data.
expected_behavior: area=timeline; setBundle (including setBundle(null) and reset) initialises laneVisibility with one true entry per source and clears the incident selection, brush range, solo and both caches, and increments timelineGeneration so a build started under the old generation cannot publish. Setting or clearing the brush range, muting a lane, changing the solo and selecting an incident all invalidate the bucket and entry caches; putBuckets keeps at most 32 keys and putEntries at most 128, evicting the oldest; replaceIncidents swaps the incident list on the existing bundle in place.
entry_points: Timeline workspace > lane chips, brush, incident chips; New/Empty Timeline
test_method: component_test: sets bundle and initializes laneVisibility from sources

title: Timeline backend queries: entries, buckets, incident detail
user_story: As an analyst I want paged rows, lane buckets and incident evidence for the current window.
expected_behavior: area=timeline; build_timeline_cmd indexes the requested sources and stores the timeline plus its per-source parser runtimes under the bundle id. query_timeline_entries_cmd returns at most the requested number of entries (the UI asks for 1000) within an optional inclusive [lo, hi] range and optional source set, sorted by timestamp then (source index, entry index), re-materialising each log line from its recorded byte offset (64 KiB per line) and dropping an entry whose file can no longer be read; query_lane_buckets_cmd returns per-lane buckets with total/error/warn counts (defaulting to the bundle's span); query_incident_details_cmd returns the incident with its signals and per-source counts, and notFound when the timeline or incident id is unknown.
entry_points: IPC: build_timeline_cmd, query_timeline_entries_cmd, query_lane_buckets_cmd, query_incident_details_cmd
notes: Full log text is not retained in memory; rows are re-materialised from file offsets on demand.

title: Timeline build validation and per-source failures
user_story: As an analyst I want an empty or oversized timeline refused and unreadable sources reported.
expected_behavior: area=timeline; build_timeline returns TimelineError::NoSources for an empty request; as soon as the running total exceeds the 5,000,000-entry limit it returns TimelineError::TooLarge { estimated, limit }; a source that cannot be read is recorded as a SourceError { path, message } on the bundle and the remaining sources still contribute; each source gets a colour from the eight-entry palette by index and a display name defaulting to the file name; a directory is treated as an IntuneEvents source only when it yields IME events; and the bundle carries the discovered [min, max] time range and total entry count.
entry_points: IPC: build_timeline_cmd
notes: DEFAULT_ENTRY_LIMIT = 5_000_000; classify_folder accepts .log/.cmtlog/.txt and the setupact/setupapi log names, and adds an IME folder when AgentExecutor.log or IntuneManagementExtension.log is present.

title: Incident detection from signals and tunables
user_story: As an analyst I want incidents derived from cross-source failure signals with a defensible confidence.
expected_behavior: area=timeline; Signals are emitted only for the enabled kinds: severity-error log lines, lines flagged as carrying an error code, and Intune events whose status is failed and which have a start time. Clusters group signals within overlapWindowMs (default 5000) and are bounded by maxIncidentSpanMs (default 60000); a cluster qualifies only when it spans at least minSourceCount (default 2) distinct sources. Confidence scores 0 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 0.85 for 1 / 2 / 3 / 4+ sources plus up to 0.24 for GUID matches and 0.10 for density, capped at 1.0. A failed Intune event supplies the anchor event reference and, when its normalized GUID is not in deniedGuids, the anchor GUID, which stamps "(correlated)" onto other signals whose materialized message contains the same GUID. The summary is "<event kind> failed: <display name>" for an anchor, otherwise "<N> signals across <M> sources".
entry_points: Timeline build (automatic); TimelineTunables.overlapWindowMs / minSourceCount / maxIncidentSpanMs / enabledSignalKinds

title: Update incident tunables in place
user_story: As an analyst I want to re-detect incidents with different thresholds without rebuilding the timeline.
expected_behavior: area=timeline; update_timeline_tunables_cmd re-runs the cached raw signals with the supplied TimelineTunables (enabled signal kinds, overlap window, minimum source count, maximum incident span) against the existing timeline's IME events and denied GUIDs, stores the new incidents on the timeline and returns them; an unknown timeline id returns notFound { id }. No frontend action calls this command, so the "gear menu" the empty incident chip bar refers to is not implemented.
entry_points: IPC: update_timeline_tunables_cmd
notes: static-only: the redetect path is exercised only through incidents.rs unit tests for redetect_from_signals; the command itself has no test and no UI caller
test_method: e2e_browser: stories/timeline-events.spec.ts :: [TL-018] no front-end action reaches update_timeline_tunables_cmd

expected_behavior: After discovery the "Discovered environment" strip shows Collector = Supported/Unavailable, ConfigMgr = the version string or "Not reported", and Observed roles chips (Client, Site Server, Management Point, Distribution Point, Software Update Point, WSUS, Provider, Admin Service, PXE Distribution Point, Certificate Registration Point, Reporting Services Point, CMG Connection Point, Service Connection Point, Client Notification Server, Unclassified candidate) each with basis Registry/Service/CIM, or "No SCCM roles observed". user_story: As a Windows admin I want capture refused with an explanation when discovery finds no ConfigMgr roles so that I do not produce an empty bundle.
expected_behavior: When discovery returns supported true with an empty roles list the workspace renders the "No SCCM roles detected" panel ("This host is supported, but discovery found no Configuration Manager roles to collect.") and disables "Capture diagnostic bundle" because canCapture requires discovery.supported && discovery.roles.length > 0. The zustand beginCapture action also refuses the capturing transition in that state.
entry_points: "Capture diagnostic bundle" (disabled); store action beginCapture
notes: extends SCCM-001 and SCCM-002
test_method: component_test: keeps capture unavailable when discovery finds no SCCM roles

title: Native failure banner preserves the last discovery
user_story: As a Windows admin I want a failed native call stated plainly while my earlier discovery stays on screen so that I can retry without losing context.
expected_behavior: Any rejected SCCM IPC call sets a store error and the workspace renders a role="alert" banner "Native operation failed" with the message, falling back to "SCCM environment discovery failed.", "SCCM diagnostic capture failed." or "Advanced SCCM capture failed." when the error carries no message; the previous discovery, ledger and capture receipt remain visible and phase returns to ready. While phase is discovering, capturing, authorizing or capturingAdvanced every button is disabled and the acting button shows a Spinner with label "Discovering environment", "Capturing bundle", "Authorizing" or "Capturing".
entry_points: "Discover environment" / "Refresh discovery" / "Capture diagnostic bundle"; role=alert banner "Native operation failed"
notes: extends SCCM-001/002/003; store fail() keeps discovery, clears any pending capability and resets phase to ready/idle.
test_method: component_test: keeps the previous discovery visible when capture fails

title: Capture receipt reports what was retained and reveals the bundle
user_story: As a Windows admin I want a receipt for a finished capture with a way to open the bundle folder so that I can hand the evidence on.
expected_behavior: A completed capture renders the "Capture result" section with "Bundle retained" -> "N artifacts" (singular "1 artifact"), "Payload" -> formatBytes(retainedBytes) ("0 B", "512 B", "1.5 KiB", "2.0 MiB"), "Captured" -> the capturedAtUtc timestamp formatted with locale dateStyle/timeStyle medium (raw string when unparsable) and a "Reveal bundle" button that calls reveal_in_file_manager with capture.bundleRoot; a reveal failure raises the banner message "The captured bundle could not be revealed.".
entry_points: "Reveal bundle" button; IPC command reveal_in_file_manager
notes: extends SCCM-002; the reveal-failure branch has no component test.
test_method: component_test: reports retained counts and reveals a successful capture

title: Advanced bounded-source cards show provenance and hard limits
user_story: As a Windows admin I want each optional advanced source shown with its provenance and limits before I pick a directory so that I know exactly what would be read.
expected_behavior: The "02 / ADVANCED SOURCES" panel "Bounded role capture" lists each advancedSources option as a card labelled with the human card name ("OSD / PXE", "Certificate enrollment / PKI", "Reporting services", "Cloud service connection", "Client notification / BGB") plus the technical source id, a provenance line ("Observed role/path - bounded capture", "Operator-declared candidate root - role not observed; capture only" or "Unavailable on this host"), the limits line "{maxBytes} total / source", "{maxFiles} files", "current + LO_", and a "Choose candidate root" button that is disabled for blocked options or while native work is in flight; the panel header counts "N allow-listed".
entry_points: "Choose candidate root"; "02 / ADVANCED SOURCES"; IPC command discover_sccm_environment (advancedSources)
notes: extends SCCM-003; options mirror the six ADVANCED_SOURCE_CONTRACTS with maxBytes 4 MiB and maxFiles 2.
test_method: component_test: runs picker consent authorization and single-use advanced capture

title: Two-step consent drives authorize then capture for one bounded source
user_story: As a Windows admin I want to choose an exact root and accept the size/file budget before any bounded advanced capture runs so that operator consent is explicit.
expected_behavior: Choosing a card opens the native directory picker open({directory:true,multiple:false}); a cancelled selection is a no-op. Confirming "Retain at most <bytes> across <n> exact current/LO_ files?" calls authorize_sccm_advanced_capture with cardId, cardVersion, sourceId, roleScope, pathClass, expectedSourceVersion and selectedRoot; on success the panel shows role="status" "Single-use authorization ready" and a second confirm "Authorization is ready. Capture this bounded source now?" runs capture_sccm_advanced_diagnostics with the capability handle and completes the capture receipt. The selected directory is never rendered, logged or stored in the workspace.
entry_points: window.confirm "Retain at most ... exact current/LO_ files?"; "Single-use authorization ready"; IPC commands authorize_sccm_advanced_capture and capture_sccm_advanced_diagnostics
notes: extends SCCM-003; the path crosses the IPC boundary only inside the authorization request.
test_method: component_test: runs picker consent authorization and single-use advanced capture

title: Unused advanced capabilities are cancelled on decline, unmount or operation replacement
user_story: As a Windows admin I want an unused authorization dropped as soon as I decline or leave so that no single-use capability lingers.
expected_behavior: Declining the second confirm clears the capability and calls cancel_sccm_advanced_capture(capabilityHandle); unmounting the workspace or starting a replacement operation bumps the operation counter and cancels any not-yet-consumed capability, and the late result is discarded without overwriting the newer state.
entry_points: window.confirm "Authorization is ready. Capture this bounded source now?" -> Cancel; component unmount; starting a second "Choose candidate root" operation
notes: extends SCCM-003; advancedOperationRef plus mountedRef gate every late continuation.
test_method: component_test: cancels a capability when final consent is declined

title: Evidence ledger separates coverage state from detail code
user_story: As a Windows admin I want the coverage ledger to distinguish state from the underlying detail so that "Capped" and "Unsafe path rejected" are not conflated.
expected_behavior: The "03 / SOURCE COVERAGE" panel "Evidence ledger" shows an "N rows" count and a table with Source, Role, Rotation (Current, LO_, Numbered, Timestamped, Unknown), State (Captured, Absent, Access denied, Capped, Skipped, Unsupported, Parse failed with a per-state icon and an em dash for Absent/Skipped) and Retained bytes via formatBytes; when detailCode is present and its label differs from the state label it is shown beneath the state (Access denied, Byte limit exceeded, File limit exceeded, Malformed rotation, Read failed, Unsafe path rejected, Unsupported platform). With no rows the panel renders "No allow-listed SCCM sources were observed for the detected roles."
entry_points: "03 / SOURCE COVERAGE"; "Evidence ledger" table
notes: extends SCCM-004
test_method: component_test: renders discovered roles and every explicit source coverage state

title: discover_sccm_environment is read-only and fails with a generic code
user_story: As a Windows admin I want discovery to touch nothing on disk and to fail with a plain code so that a failed probe cannot leak host detail.
expected_behavior: discover_sccm_environment returns the public SccmEnvironmentDiscovery (supported, configmgrVersion, sorted and deduped roles, empty sources, issues, advancedSources) without creating any file; PrivateSccmEnvironment fields (private_host, private_site_code, capture roots, advanced source facts) are never serialized. A provider failure becomes AppError::Analysis("discoveryFailed") and every collector error surfaces only as its code string: discoveryFailed, noRolesDetected, destinationUnavailable, captureFailed, manifestValidationFailed, advancedAuthorizationRejected, advancedCapabilityUnavailable.
entry_points: IPC command discover_sccm_environment
notes: normalize_public_discovery sorts roles by role key and basis, dedups roles and issues, and sort_sources orders by role/sourceId/rotation/state.

title: Capture writes a private UUID bundle and a parser-validated client manifest
user_story: As a Windows admin I want each capture to land in its own private bundle folder with a manifest the parser already accepts.
expected_behavior: capture_sccm_diagnostics resolves the app cache dir, creates <cache>/sccm with mode 0700 on unix, and writes into a fresh <cache>/sccm/<uuid> bundle containing sccm-manifest.json with provenance nativeClientCapture, provenanceProfile hmacSha256V1, maxFilesPerSource/maxBytesPerSource, fingerprint-derived artifactIds, per-source contentSha256 and fragmentComplete false when capped; the writer then re-opens the bundle with read_sccm_client_intake_bundle so a manifest the reader rejects is never reported as success.
entry_points: IPC command capture_sccm_diagnostics
platforms: all (native collector; live discovery is Windows-only)
notes: extends SCCM-002; MAX_FRAGMENTS_PER_SOURCE 8 and MAX_BYTES_PER_SOURCE 16 MiB are recorded in the manifest envelope.

title: Capture refuses unsupported or role-less hosts before writing
user_story: As a Windows admin I want a capture attempt on a host with nothing to collect to fail before any directory is created.
expected_behavior: When the provider reports supported false or an empty role list, capture fails with noRolesDetected and neither <cache>/sccm nor a bundle directory exists afterwards, because the role check runs before destination preparation; the same check is repeated for an already-discovered environment.
entry_points: IPC command capture_sccm_diagnostics
notes: SccmCollectorError::NoRolesDetected is the shared code for both the unsupported and empty-role cases.

title: Advanced authorization is strict, bounded, single-use and expiring
user_story: As a Windows admin I want the advanced authorization endpoint to accept only exact contract fields and to hand out one short-lived, cancelable ticket.
expected_behavior: SccmAdvancedCaptureAuthorizationRequest denies unknown fields; authorize_sccm_advanced_capture rejects a request that does not match cardId+cardVersion+sourceId+roleScope+pathClass, an expectedSourceVersion that differs from the discovered ConfigMgr version, a duplicate pending authorization for the same contract/root/provenance, and any new request once eight capabilities are pending. The issued handle is consumable once, cancelable, expires after five minutes, purges expired entries before each operation, and nothing is persisted across restarts.
entry_points: IPC commands authorize_sccm_advanced_capture and cancel_sccm_advanced_capture
notes: ADVANCED_CAPABILITY_LIMIT 8, ADVANCED_CAPABILITY_TTL 300s; handles are capability/authorization sha256 v1 tokens.

title: Advanced capture roots must be real directories and not links
user_story: As a Windows admin I want a selected root that is a link or not a directory rejected before it is remembered.
expected_behavior: validate_selected_root rejects empty, untrimmed, NUL-bearing or glob-bearing selections and any path whose symlink_metadata shows a symlink, a reparse point or a non-directory, returning advancedAuthorizationRejected without storing a capability; the canonicalized path is what the authorization binds to and hashes into the handle.
entry_points: IPC command authorize_sccm_advanced_capture
notes: a hostile symlinked observed fact also falls back to operator-declared provenance rather than observed.

title: Non-Windows discovery reports an unsupported collector
user_story: As an analyst running on macOS or Linux I want discovery to say the collector is unsupported instead of guessing roles.
expected_behavior: On a non-Windows host discover_sccm_environment returns supported false with exactly one unsupportedPlatform issue and no roles or sources; roles are reported only from explicit facts and are never inferred from a default path, and the public result is deterministic for equal input.
entry_points: IPC command discover_sccm_environment
platforms: all (only the Windows branch performs the live probe)
notes: discover_native is #[cfg(not(target_os = "windows"))] returning the unsupported environment with SccmDiscoveryIssueCode::UnsupportedPlatform.

title: Windows discovery uses registry roles and one fixed CIM service query
user_story: As a Windows admin I want role discovery based on documented registry keys plus one fixed service query so that nothing is guessed and no service path leaks.
expected_behavior: Discovery reads HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\CCM\Setup (Client role and ProductVersion), HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\SMS\Setup (Site Server, Site Code, Installation Directory->Logs) and HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\SMS\{MP,DP,SUP,WSUS,Providers,AdminService} for each role's Log Directory, recording registryAccessDenied when a hive is refused. It then runs one fixed PowerShell command ($ErrorActionPreference='Stop'; Get-CimInstance -Namespace 'root/cimv2' -ClassName Win32_Service -Filter "Name='CcmExec' OR Name='SMS_EXECUTIVE' OR Name='SMS_ADMIN_SERVICE' OR Name='WSUSService'" | Select-Object Name,PathName | ConvertTo-Json -Compress), mapping a nonzero exit to cimAccessDenied and a launch failure to discoveryFailed; the client capture root is derived from the CcmExec PathName (quotes and trailing arguments tolerated, wrappers/relative/UNC/wrong basename rejected) and serialized discovery never contains the service path.
entry_points: IPC command discover_sccm_environment
notes: role_for_cim_service maps only those four service names; role roots fall back from Log Directory to site install Logs to a default location, with origin recorded.

title: BGB advanced source requires a matching Management Point role and configured root
user_story: As a Windows admin I want the Client notification / BGB source offered as observed only when a Management Point role and its configured log root both exist.
expected_behavior: assemble_native_environment clears any provider-supplied advanced facts and re-derives the single advanced-client-notification-bgb fact only from a Management Point role plus a ConfiguredRoleLogDirectory root; service-derived, site-install-fallback or symlinked roots never qualify and the card falls back to "Operator-declared candidate root". Sources flagged requires_pxe_fact (OSD / PXE) additionally require an explicitly enabled PXE fact to count as observed.
entry_points: "Choose candidate root" (Client notification / BGB and OSD / PXE cards)
notes: extends SCCM-003

title: Capture reports caps and non-captured states for every expected source
user_story: As a Windows admin I want a per-source coverage row even when nothing could be retained so that missing evidence is coverage, not health.
expected_behavior: Enumeration emits a row for every expected allow-listed source: missing files become Absent, a symlink or reparse-point entry becomes Skipped with unsafePath, an unparsable rotation filename becomes Unsupported with malformedRotation, an unreadable file becomes AccessDenied or ParseFailed with accessDenied/readFailed, and exceeding MAX_FRAGMENTS_PER_SOURCE (8) or MAX_BYTES_PER_SOURCE (16 MiB) yields Capped with fileLimitExceeded/byteLimitExceeded while retainedBytes is the exact copied prefix. The same basename under two roots stays two distinct rows, an uncatalogued file such as Mtrmgr.log is never admitted, and copy uses a no-follow open with canonical-path containment plus exclusive create and a per-artifact sha256.
entry_points: IPC command capture_sccm_diagnostics (evidence ledger rows)
notes: extends SCCM-004: these rows are what the workspace ledger renders. Root enumeration failures are recorded against every expected source with coverage scope RootEnumeration.

title: Task Sequence provenance is sealed only for physical smsts rotations
user_story: As an analyst I want smsts.log provenance expressed as an opaque path class plus relocation ordinal so that task-sequence capture is traceable without exporting machine paths.
expected_behavior: A physical smsts.log row (current or lo_) carries taskSequenceProvenance with version 1, pathClass client, the closed token synthetic:smsts-path:client, a relocation lineage hash and relocationOrdinal; the reader rejects missing, tampered or path-class-mismatched provenance, rejects provenance attached to non-task-sequence artifacts, and coverage-only markers carry none, while current and lo_ rotations share one relocation without colliding.
entry_points: IPC command capture_sccm_diagnostics; read_sccm_client_intake_bundle
notes: SCCM_TASK_SEQUENCE_PROVENANCE_VERSION 1; the evidence token is a reviewed closed value, never a raw path.

title: Server manifest redacts paths and is parser-validated before success
user_story: As a site administrator I want server captures to record roles, handles and coverage with originalPath REDACTED so that a bundle can be shared without exposing machine paths.
expected_behavior: For any non-client role, capture writes sccm-server-manifest.json with bundleRole "server", privacy.rawPaths "redacted", hashed captureHost/siteCode handles, per-artifact artifactId/sourceId/sourceKind/rotation lineage/capture state/limits/bytesCopied and originalPath "REDACTED"; WSUS rows add an instance handle and a pinned sourceVersion, and coverage rows carry an opaque collectionDetail, skipReason or unsupportedReason depending on state. The JSON is fed back through normalize_server_bundle and a rejection fails the capture with manifestValidationFailed; a capped server file reopens as Capped with its limits preserved and no payload.
entry_points: IPC command capture_sccm_diagnostics
notes: SCCM_SERVER_MANIFEST_FILE_NAME is sccm-server-manifest.json; the manifest is only written when at least one non-client role was observed.

title: Capture refuses to overwrite an existing bundle
user_story: As a Windows admin I want collection to refuse a bundle path that already exists instead of merging into it.
expected_behavior: prepare_private_bundle_root creates the bundle directory exclusively and preflight_destinations rejects any duplicate relative destination or one that already exists on disk with destinationUnavailable, so a second capture never writes into an existing tree and never follows a pre-planted link.
entry_points: IPC command capture_sccm_diagnostics
notes: advanced capture uses the same exclusive bundle creation rule.

title: Manifest reader binds reads to a verified private root handle
user_story: As a security reviewer I want bundle reads bound to a verified private directory handle so that a swapped or planted file cannot be read.
expected_behavior: verify_bundle_root opens the bundle root without following links, requires a real directory owned by the capture user (or root/LocalSystem/BuiltinAdministrators) with no group/other permission bits on unix and a DACL granting only restricted trustees on Windows, then resolves sccm-manifest.json and every evidence file component-by-component relative to that handle, rejecting symlinks, reparse points, non-regular files and multi-link entries; a missing final component surfaces as NotFound so the legacy fallback still runs. A non-private root, symlinked root, symlinked manifest or hard-linked evidence fails without disclosing the bundle path.
entry_points: read_sccm_manifest_or_legacy; read_sccm_client_intake_bundle
notes: unix uses openat with O_NOFOLLOW/O_DIRECTORY per component and nlink==1; Windows uses NtCreateFile with FILE_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT relative to the held handle.

title: Manifest reader bounds decoding and enforces client physical caps
user_story: As a maintainer I want the reader to bound a hostile manifest and to reject ambiguous ordering, duplicate identities or oversized physical claims before reading evidence.
expected_behavior: The reader caps the manifest file at 4 MiB and the artifacts plus capture-gaps arrays at one shared 4096-entry ceiling, rejects duplicate artifact ids and non-canonical rotation order (current, lo_, numbered, timestamped, unknown), and enforces the client-owned physical budget (256 MiB per artifact, 1 GiB total) before any evidence file is opened. A missing manifest falls back to the legacy manifest.json, which is projected as coverage without inventing native capture gaps or content bindings and without echoing the bundle path in error messages.
entry_points: read_sccm_manifest_or_legacy; read_sccm_client_intake_bundle

user_story: As an analyst I want value kinds and deletions obvious at a glance.
